title: NASA Astronauts Prepare for High-Risk Spacewalk Outside the ISS Tomorrow
excerpt: Indian-American astronaut Anil Menon and ESA's Sophie Adenot will replace a critical communications antenna during a six-and-a-half-hour spacewalk on Tuesday.
body:
• NASA astronaut Anil Menon and ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot will conduct U.S. Spacewalk 97 on Tuesday, August 18, replacing a Space-to-Ground antenna on the ISS.
  • The spacewalk will be Adenot's first ever and Menon's second, following a six-hour excursion on August 6 where a spacesuit CO2 sensor returned an unexpected reading.
  • Menon, born to a Kerala-origin father and Ukrainian mother, is the first NASA astronaut of Malayali descent to go to space.

Two astronauts aboard the International Space Station are gearing up for a spacewalk on Tuesday that will see them spend roughly six and a half hours in the vacuum of space replacing a critical communications antenna.

NASA flight engineer Anil Menon and ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot will step outside the orbital outpost for U.S. Spacewalk 97, swapping a Space-to-Ground antenna on the station's Z1 truss segment. The antenna is part of the system that maintains high-speed data and voice links between the ISS and Mission Control in Houston, according to NASA.

Preparations and a Delayed Schedule

The spacewalk was originally planned for earlier in August but was pushed to August 18 after engineers needed additional time to evaluate a spacesuit issue. During the previous spacewalk on August 6, a carbon dioxide sensor on Menon's suit returned an unexpected data reading. Menon reported no other issues, and the sensor returned to normal after the suit was removed, but NASA opted to assess whether to change suits before proceeding, according to a NASA blog post.

https://x.com/esa/status/2089269194764238974

The crew has spent the past week running through preparations. Menon and Adenot worked together inside the Quest airlock organizing the tools they will carry outside. Station commander Jessica Meir and flight engineer Jack Hathaway, both NASA astronauts, studied the Canadarm2 robotic arm maneuvers they will use to assist the spacewalkers from inside the station. Hathaway and Adenot also cleaned the cooling systems in a pair of spacesuits, according to NASA.

Adenot's First Spacewalk

Tuesday's excursion will mark Sophie Adenot's first-ever spacewalk. The French ESA astronaut arrived at the ISS in February as part of the Crew-12 mission alongside Meir, Hathaway, and Russian cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev. During her time on the station, Adenot has conducted bioprinting research, tested the EuroSuit prototype, and participated in exercise studies using the EasyMotion-2 electromyostimulation suit, according to NASA and the European Space Agency.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=awQzjn72bI0

ESA will broadcast the spacewalk live on ESA WebTV and YouTube, with coverage beginning at 13:00 CEST (4:00 a.m. PDT) and the spacewalk scheduled to start at approximately 14:35 CEST (5:35 a.m. PDT), according to ESA.

Menon's Second Trip Outside

For Menon, this will be his second spacewalk in less than two weeks. On August 6, he and commander Jessica Meir spent six hours and 27 minutes outside the station building a modification kit on the Starboard 6 truss segment, preparing it for the future installation of a roll-out solar array later this year, according to NASA.

A third spacewalk is currently planned for August 25, making this one of the busiest months for extravehicular activity on the station in recent years.

An Indian-American Astronaut's Journey

Menon's presence on the ISS carries particular significance for the Indian diaspora. Born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, to an Indian father from Kerala and a Ukrainian mother, he is the first NASA astronaut of Malayali descent to journey into space, according to the Times of India.

"Dr. Menon was SpaceX's first flight surgeon, helping to launch its first humans to space during the Demo-2 mission and building a medical organization to support the human system during future missions."

— NASA astronaut biography

Before becoming an astronaut, Menon earned degrees from Harvard and Stanford, served as a flight surgeon with the U.S. Air Force, and was a first responder during the 2010 Haiti earthquake and the 2015 Nepal earthquake. He was selected for NASA's astronaut class in 2021 and launched to the ISS aboard the Roscosmos Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft on July 14, 2026, for an eight-month mission, according to NASA.

What's Next

The Expedition 75 crew currently includes seven members: Meir, Hathaway, Adenot, and Fedyaev from Crew-12, plus Menon, Pyotr Dubrov, and Anna Kikina who arrived via Soyuz. The Crew-12 contingent is scheduled to depart in September following the arrival of Crew-13, according to USA Today.
